roster.name: Zarya (FGB)
roster.note: The first module — a US-funded, Russian-built control and power block: the seed of the entire station.

roster.name: Unity (Node 1)
roster.note: The first US module, a six-port connecting hub joined to Zarya two weeks later.

roster.name: Zvezda
roster.note: The Russian service module that made the station habitable: crew quarters, life support, and propulsion.

roster.name: Destiny
roster.note: The US laboratory — the primary research module and the station's command center.

roster.name: Canadarm2
roster.note: Canada's robotic arm, which assembled much of the station and catches arriving spacecraft.

roster.name: Quest
roster.note: The US airlock, enabling spacewalks in both American and Russian suits.

roster.name: Pirs
roster.note: A Russian docking compartment and airlock — deorbited in 2021 to make room for Nauka.

roster.name: Harmony (Node 2)
roster.note: The hub that opened the way for the international laboratories.

roster.name: Columbus
roster.note: Europe's laboratory — ESA's cornerstone contribution to the station.

roster.name: Kibo
roster.note: Japan's laboratory — the largest single module, with its own external platform.

roster.name: Poisk
roster.note: A Russian docking and airlock module on Zvezda's zenith.

roster.name: Tranquility (Node 3)
roster.note: Life support and exercise equipment — and the mount for the Cupola.

roster.name: Cupola
roster.note: The seven-windowed observation dome, source of the station's most famous views of Earth.

roster.name: Rassvet
roster.note: A Russian docking and storage module.

roster.name: Leonardo (PMM)
roster.note: A permanent storage module, converted from a reusable cargo carrier.

roster.name: BEAM
roster.note: An experimental inflatable module, testing expandable habitats in orbit.

roster.name: Nauka
roster.note: The long-delayed Russian science module, added more than two decades after assembly began.

roster.name: Prichal
roster.note: A Russian docking node — among the most recent additions.

roster.name: Expedition 1
roster.note: the first resident crew arrived 2 November 2000; humans have lived aboard continuously ever since — the longest unbroken human presence off Earth in history

roster.name: Commercial Crew
roster.note: SpaceX's Crew Dragon restored US crew launch after nine years, beginning the handover of low-orbit access to commercial providers
